rationale: At the 8.49 ns floor all four runs pass with +0.40..+0.53 ns at ss 100C 1.60V max-RC. Hold (+0.09, no buffers), slew/cap (<=37 vs 953) and final DRC never bind. Raising margins from 0.2/0.3 to 0.35/0.4 gained only ~0.02 ns, so the repair target is saturated. The limit looks wire-related: the max-RC corner limits, routed length is ~15% over the estimate, and the worst path switches between port and reg-to-reg within 0.05 ns. The optimizer sets every boolean false, so pin two untried wire-delay levers: timing-driven placement (shortens critical and port nets) and post-GRT design repair (rebuffers long routed nets under cap213). Keep 0.45, cap213, post-GRT timing, DELAY 4, util 30, dd 24. Margins are freed because history keeps them high.
